## The range, and the arithmetic, and the one thing you may not assume

**Volume 09 is fifty chapters on fifty days, days 401 to 450, one chapter to one day, and it is finished. The hundred and thirty-fifth day of the Bare Month was day 450, a Wednesday, and it is the last day of that month any chapter of this volume printed, and no chapter printed a day after it.** Day 400 was a Tuesday and the eighty-fifth day of that month, and day 401 was a Wednesday and the eighty-sixth.

**RECOMPUTE THE FIFTY DAYS FROM DAY 1 BEING A TUESDAY before you write a word, and check all fifty against your own arithmetic and against `outline/volume-09.md` §14.3, and if your arithmetic and a table disagree your arithmetic is right.** The run was validated five times in this volume, once at the start of each batch, at zero mismatches every time, and each of the five batches re-ran it before any prose was written rather than after. **A weekday on a page outranks a weekday in a plan, and a day map is a plan.**

**AND THE BARE MONTH.** It was registered with **NO STATED LENGTH** by a notary of fifty who named it on a page in Chapter 0316 and said why, and the reason is hers. **It did not end inside this volume and no chapter of this volume ended it, and no chapter attached a meaning to the hundredth, the hundred and twentieth or the hundred and thirty-fifth.** **YOU MAY NOT END IT, YOU MAY NOT GIVE IT A LENGTH, AND YOU MAY NOT LET THE CLOSE RECORD BE THE PLACE WHERE IT LOOKS LIKE IT HAS ONE.** If whatever comes next needs the end of the Bare Month on a page, **that is a thing a person does in a room, in daylight, with a date on the door, and it is the next volume's first decision and not this record's.** Note that Volume 09 wrote inside the Bare Month for eighty-six to a hundred and thirty-five days, which is nearly half of a month of no known length, and the fact that fifty chapters fit inside it without approaching an end is the strongest evidence this repository has that the device works.

## The four decisions this phase takes, and where they go

1. **THE VOICE OF THE NEXT VOLUME, confirmed or not, and if it is confirmed say so in a sentence and say what carries.** Seven volumes have confirmed it: fifty-day volumes, one chapter to one day, about a page and a yard and a wage in salt, nobody gets stronger. **Add to it what this volume found about the shape of a sentence, and this volume found more about that than any volume before it, and you must publish the numbers, not the impression.**
   - **The collapse and the repair.** Batch 0005's ten files stood at a batch mean of 53 words to the sentence, per-chapter means from 67 to 186, a longest single sentence of 136 words, and three constructions that had taken the volume over: a narrator's *about four people … have worked out since that* at 11 across ten chapters, the chain *and nobody in that room* at 46 stacked three deep in one sentence in several places, and five chapters in ten closing on the same two clauses. **The repair pass rebuilt all ten files out of the sentences they already had and did not add a fact, a day, a count or an event: 26 words to the sentence, per-chapter means 22 to 33, a longest sentence of 79, the same two hundred and sixty-nine words of *nobody* chains cut to thirty-two, and four per cent shorter and not thinner.** **Write that down as a transferable finding and not as a story about this batch: a repair pass can rebuild fifty sentences without touching fifty facts, and the test that it has not is not a word count, it is that the day run, the counts, the object inventory, the cast placements and the prohibitions all re-assert against the strings afterwards.**
   - **A habit is a rule's job and not a warning's.** Two instruments both returning a figure a writer expected is not two instruments. **Add the third: a prose fault that five batches of warnings did not remove is a rule, and the rule has to be written into the prose instructions, and the way to know it is a habit rather than a fault is that it has a count — nineteen rates, sixteen posts, eleven withies, about four people, about nine people, about nine yards, nine steps, four hundred miles — and a set of numbers that recurs is a rhythm the reader learns whether or not the writer meant it.**
   - **A finding the review raised and the close should confirm or reject: the protagonist is in nine chapters of fifty and in both of Batch 0005's ten he is furniture.** The review is right that this is thin and right that the remedy is a decision and not a repair, and **`outline/volume-09.md` §4 is the decision that produced it, nine chapters, one of which is a morning on which he reads nothing and nobody asks him anything and nobody declines to ask him anything, and a chapter may put him somewhere and let him watch and must then not say he was right.** **Say in your close record plainly whether that rule has now cost the volume its protagonist across two volumes, because that is a real finding about a rule and not an aesthetic preference, and it belongs in the brief of whatever plans the next one.**

Do not print them and do not assert that they are in no file, and if you find yourself writing a sentence that certifies an absence, check it on the files before you write it.**

## The house figures for the volume, gathered, with the definitions beside them and no target on any of them

**Gather the five batch records' §3 tables into one table, per batch, and publish the range and the mean of the fifty with both conventions named, and say once and only once that the mean is a consequence and not a plan and that no review may certify or fail this volume on one.** The bolded share across the five batches runs from 5.97 in Batch 0001's range to 22.82 in Batch 0004's, and after the Batch 0005 repair the last ten run 6.24 to 21.81 with an unweighted mean of 13.85. **The longest bolded turn in the last ten is seventy-seven words, in Chapter 0448, and the hard ceiling is ninety-five, and that figure did not move in the repair and must not be read as having been touched.** The count of paragraphs carrying neither speaker marker is zero in all ten of the last batch and was zero after the repair. **The exchange is a consequence and not a target, and the last batch's twenty-two marked turns across thirty-six plain speech paragraphs is lower than the batch before it, and the reason is that four of its ten chapters are a road and a barrow and a rope and a chair and not a room with two people in it.** **Publish the sentence-length figures for the last ten, before and after, because they are the only measure in this repository that caught the fault the review found and none of the seven checks in §20 does that work.**

**And close out the object inventory at `outline/volume-09.md` §20.6, which the Batch 0005 review repair pass corrected against the files in six places and whose second column never moved: the sheet at one, with four places and the third empty on all fifty days; the notices at seven and no eighth; the fence at sixteen willow posts and eleven withies bound with the same cord; one register with three columns and the third empty on purpose and one line entered in it in this volume; one second slate, untouched in all fifty; the party and the road at four, three, one and three barrows; the three four-place forms, never joined; one piece of chalk in an inside breast pocket, not taken out since day 298; a date in chalk on the door in every chapter; one length of new rope, never used; about four hundred and forty, of which one figure is on no page and is printed nowhere; and four hundred miles.** Publish it as a table with the chapters that named each, because a set of objects counted in two chapters is counted by no check in this repository and this volume's last image is three barrows on a road.
